rationale: spectral-norm is a tiny, compute-bound numeric kernel (542 lines, 6 functions, ~1.7KB text) whose hot path is dense floating-point arithmetic (eval_A via multiply-subtract expressions) inside tight iteration loops, so the table favors cheap data-oriented transforms and penalizes control-flow-heavy ones: SUB and SPLIT get high security/diversity weights with negligible cost/risk weights since arithmetic substitution and basic-block splitting add strong expression-level obfuscation at near-zero overhead, while FLA is suppressed with the highest RuntimeCost weight (0.9) because flattening dispatch loops in floating-point kernels typically causes severe slowdowns on such small functions, and BCF is kept moderate with elevated runtime/size cost weights since bogus arithmetic inside hot loops hurts without proportional security gain for a program this small; IBR and IGV sit at moderate values to add indirection diversity where features support it without dominating decisions, and ICALL is weighted toward cost/risk because indirect-call conversion in a program with almost no call sites offers little diversity benefit while its dispatch overhead lands directly in the hot numeric loops; correctness-risk weights stay low overall since all seven passes are semantics-preserving on this straight-line FP code, but higher for ICALL/IGV/FLA where indirect dispatch on small functions carries the most transformation sensitivity.
